text:
This looks like December 2020. The unemployment rate is 6.7%, which matches November/December 2020. The fed funds rate is 0.09% and the 10-year yield is 0.93%, both consistent with late 2020. The VIX at 22.77 fits December, since it was about 20-23 then. Gold rose 4.8% over the month, which fits December 2020 (gold went from about 1777 to 1895). The 10-year yield rose 0.24 over 3 months, from about 0.69 to 0.93, which also fits.

Industrial production YoY of -5.5% fits November 2020. The unemployment rate of 6.7% was the November reading, published in early December. Payrolls averaging +522k over three months is also consistent with the September to November period. The data were therefore published through November, but the market data run to the end of the month. The snapshot describes end-November or end-December 2020.

Equity returns point to November, when US large-cap gained about 11% and emerging markets rose around 9%. The 1m US equity return here is only +2.6%, which suggests December (S&P 500 up 3.8% in December). The 10-year yield at the end of November was about 0.84, versus 0.93 at the end of December. On that basis I choose December 2020.
